claims.scope: Limit order matching in CLOB._processLimitBidOrder/_processLimitAskOrder where a zero-amount guard uses bit-wise AND

preconditions.text: A taker submits a matching buy (BID) with amountInBase = 1 and quoteAmount = 2.; The zero-amount guard in _processLimitBidOrder and _processLimitAskOrder uses bit-wise AND on baseTokenAmountReceived and quoteTokenAmountSent.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: 2. Taker submits a matching buy (BID) with `amountInBase = 1` and `quoteAmount = 2`.

Instead, `baseTokenAmountReceived & quoteTokenAmountSent` performs a bit-level comparison. Two **non-zero** integers that share no common set bits (e.g., `1` and `2`) pass this test, so the compound condition becomes true whenever the amounts differ and have no overlapping bits. In practice:

safety.text: Inferred: the zero-amount guard should reject a trade only when either side is actually zero, allowing legitimate non-zero trades to complete.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: [`_processLimitBidOrder()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-07-gte-clob/blob/2783108d14010ae50f2a5f65c3a9c94e2e7845b9/contracts/clob/CLOB.sol#L492-L531) and [`_processLimitAskOrder()`](https://github.com/code-423n4/2025-07-gte-clob/blob/2783108d14010ae50f2a5f65c3a9c94e2e7845b9/contracts/clob/CLOB.sol#L533-L571) use a bit-wise AND (`&`) instead of a logical check to detect zero-amount trades, causing legitimate trades to revert with `ZeroCostTrade`.
The developer’s intention is to throw when either side of the trade is zero.

effects.text: Because 1 != 2 and 1 & 2 == 0, ZeroCostTrade() reverts, aborting the otherwise valid match.
